mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with 3-month FEDFUNDS decline, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales indicate contracting consumer demand that reduces corporate revenue expectations, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production during early recession phases reduces manufacturing output and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p>0.05) during early recession when INDPRO declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL increase above 2.0% signals rising inflation that triggers Federal Reserve tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 2 years.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate above 4.5% indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 2 years.

mechanism_narrative: In low-unemployment labor markets, a sharp decline in non-farm payrolls signals impending economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p>0.05) in low-unemployment labor markets when PAYEMS declines sharply, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production over 3 months indicates manufacturing sector weakness that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with 3-month INDPRO decline, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 3 years.
